content:
lee: hey team, first day here 👋 trying to run the dev docker image to build the runtime but inside the container `nvidia-smi` says 'No devices found'. stuck.

lee: command I'm using:
```
docker run --gpus all -it --rm -v $(pwd):/src redwood/dev-runtime:cuda-12.1 bash
```

lee: host `nvidia-smi` shows GPU 0: A100-SXM4 Driver 525.116, but inside container nothing. also docker errors sometimes: `could not select device driver \"nvidia\" with capabilities: [[gpu]]`. who should I ping for container GPU setup?

arjun: hey @lee, welcome! that error usually means the NVIDIA Container Toolkit or the daemon runtime isn't configured. quick checks: `which nvidia-container-runtime` on host and check `/etc/docker/daemon.json`.

lee: outputs:
```
$ which nvidia-container-runtime
/usr/bin/nvidia-container-runtime

$ cat /etc/docker/daemon.json
{}
```

kira: on corp GPU hosts we set default-runtime to nvidia in daemon.json. if this is a personal cloud VM you spun up, you can add the runtime and restart docker: 
```
sudo mkdir -p /etc/docker && sudo tee /etc/docker/daemon.json <<'EOF'
{"runtimes":{"nvidia":{"path":"nvidia-container-runtime","runtimeArgs":[]}},"default-runtime":"nvidia"}
EOF
sudo systemctl restart docker
```

infra-bot: notice: changing /etc/docker/daemon.json requires host admin privileges. If this VM is managed by infra, open ticket INFRA-3421. For ephemeral dev, it's OK to change your personal VM.

lee: applied the daemon.json change and restarted docker. `docker run --gpus all` now starts but inside container I get permission denied accessing `/dev/nvidiactl` and `ls -l /dev/nvidia*` shows devices owned by root:video and my user isn't in video group.

arjun: add your user to the video group or adjust udev rules. `sudo usermod -aG video $USER` then log out/in. For CI we use udev rules so containers inherit appropriate perms.

kira: workaround if you can't re-login: run container with `--device /dev/nvidia0:/dev/nvidia0` and `--group-add video` or use the `--privileged` flag temporarily (not recommended).

lee: added to video group and re-logged in. container now sees GPUs, thanks! build starts but fails during pip install: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pybind11'` when compiling our C++ bindings.

dev-tools: we vendor pybind11 in third_party but the bootstrap step copies it into wheelhouse. Did you run `scripts/bootstrap-dev-env.sh`? If not, run it or `pip install pybind11==2.9.1` in your venv.

lee: ran bootstrap script, that populated third_party and pip deps. build moves on but unit tests fail trying to bind to `/tmp/rt-socket` with permission denied.

arjun: tests expect the runtime test dir to be writable by developer group. run `mkdir -p /tmp/rt-socket && chmod 770 /tmp/rt-socket && chgrp video /tmp/rt-socket` or run `bazel test` via `scripts/test-wrapper.sh` which sets up the sandbox for you.

lee: did that, tests pass locally now. I'll open a tiny onboarding PR with steps I needed: docker daemon.json snippet, add note about adding user to video group, and remind to run bootstrap script. tagging @kira for docs review.

kira: please add the snippet and reference ticket INFRA-3421 for infra-managed hosts. Also add a note about the recommended dev image `redwood/dev-runtime:cuda-12.1` and the ephemeral GPU host we spin up for new hires. :tada:

infra-bot: created ephemeral GPU dev host `gpu-dev-lee-7` for 48 hours. Use with caution; it will be auto-terminated.

lee: huge thanks everyone — feeling unblocked. will push the doc PR and the small follow-up to dev-tools if we need to make bootstrap more obvious. excited to be here! :grinning:
